key_insight: A 2D chiral fluid can generate an antisymmetric “chiral pressure” from a parity-breaking pseudo-scalar, and this effect persists even in a homogeneous steady state.
engineering_relevance: This suggests continuum CFD models for chiral or micropolar fluids must include rotational viscosity and antisymmetric pressure terms to capture zero-gradient bulk behavior correctly.
method: Derived the microscopic expression for the chiral pressure from a parity-breaking pseudo-scalar average.
Linked the effect to micropolar hydrodynamics via the rotational (vortex) viscosity.
Computed the kinetic rotational viscosity for rough disks to Gaussian order.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an analytical microscopic derivation and a kinetic calculation, showing the chiral pressure and rotational viscosity survive at zeroth order in gradients in a well-defined Quiescent Chiral State.
watch_item: The result is specific to idealized 2D chiral/rough-disk assumptions, so direct use in 3D or non-micropolar CFD models may miss the antisymmetric stress contribution.
paper_title: Microscopic origin of the chiral pressure in a two-dimensional fluid
